## Update build-tools image version in devcontainer and setup script

The goal is to update the pinned version of the `build-tools` container image used for development and build environments. The repository currently references a specific image tag (`master-a27b9b60db555184f332436a42268021826344f2`) in two locations. We need to synchronize these references to use the latest available version of the build-tools image, as produced by the common-files automation.

The updated image version should be applied consistently across:
- The devcontainer configuration (for VS Code development environments)
- The environment setup script (which determines the build container image for CI and local builds)

This update ensures all development and build environments use the same, current build-tools version, which may include updated dependencies, tools, and security fixes.

## Environment Setup
Review the repository's development and build configuration by examining:
    - `Makefile` and `Makefile.core.mk` for build and test targets
    - `common/Makefile.common.mk` for shared makefile logic
    - `common/scripts/setup_env.sh` for environment configuration (this is one of the files to be modified)
    - `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` for development container setup (this is another file to be modified)
    - `common/.commonfiles.sha` to understand the common-files tracking mechanism

## Implementation Plan
1. Identify the latest build-tools image version reference (likely from the common-files repository or automation output)
    2. Update the image tag in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` from the current version to the new version
    3. Update the default `IMAGE_VERSION` value in `common/scripts/setup_env.sh` from the current version to the new version
    4. Update the checksum record in `common/.commonfiles.sha` to reflect the new common-files state
    5. Verify the changes are consistent across all modified files and ensure no other references to the old image version remain

132: # This function checks if the file exists. If it does, it creates a randomly named host location
133: # for the file, adds it to the host KUBECONFIG, and creates a mount for it.
134: add_KUBECONFIG_if_exists () {
135:   if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then

142: # This function is designed for maximum compatibility with various platforms. This runs on
143: # any Mac or Linux platform with bash 4.2+. Please take care not to modify this function
144: # without testing properly.
145: #
146: # This function will properly handle any type of path including those with spaces using the
147: # loading pattern specified by *kubectl config*.
148: #
149: # testcase: "a:b c:d"
150: # testcase: "a b:c d:e f"
151: # testcase: "a b:c:d e"
152: parse_KUBECONFIG () {
153: TMPDIR=""
154: if [[ "$1" =~ ([^:]*):(.*) ]]; then
155:   while true; do
156:     rematch=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
157:     add_KUBECONFIG_if_exists "$rematch"
158:     remainder="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
159:     if [[ ! "$remainder" =~ ([^:]*):(.*) ]]; then
160:       if [[ -n "$remainder" ]]; then
161:         add_KUBECONFIG_if_exists "$remainder"

163:       fi
164:     fi
165:   done
166: else

168: fi

# Ztunnel

Ztunnel provides an experimental implementation of the ztunnel component of
[ambient mesh](https://istio.io/latest/blog/2022/introducing-ambient-mesh/).

Note: `istio/ztunnel` is currently intended for experimental usage only.

## Feature Scope

Ztunnel is intended to be a purpose built implementation of the node proxy in [ambient mesh](https://istio.io/latest/blog/2022/introducing-ambient-mesh/).
Part of the goals of this included keeping a narrow feature set, implementing only the bare minimum requirements for ambient.
This ensures the project remains simple and high performance.

Explicitly out of scope for ztunnel include:
* Terminating user HTTP traffic
* Terminating user HTTP traffic (its worth repeating)
* Generic extensibility such as `ext_authz`, WASM, linked-in extensions, Lua, etc.

In general, ztunnel does not aim to be a generic extensible proxy; Envoy is better suited for that task.
If a feature is not directly used to implement the node proxy component in ambient mesh, it is unlikely to be accepted.

## Building

### FIPS

Ztunnel builds currently enable the `fips` Cargo feature by default, which in turn enables the `fips` feature
on [BoringSSL](https://github.com/cloudflare/boring).

FIPS has
[strict requirements](https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/documents/security-policies/140sp4407.pdf)

The goal is to implement a mechanism that tracks open inbound and inbound-passthrough connections and closes them when an authorization policy update makes them invalid. This requires:

    - A new connection manager component that tracks active connections.
    - Notification to the connection manager when authorization policies change.
    - A background task that reacts to policy change notifications and closes now-denied connections.
    - Integration of this tracking into inbound, inbound-passthrough, outbound, and SOCKS5 proxy paths.

    The primary user-facing behavior is that when an RBAC policy change (e.g., `allow -> deny`) takes effect, existing connections that violate the new policy are terminated instead of continuing to pass traffic.

## Environment Setup
The repository is a Rust workspace. Key configuration files for setting up the environment and understanding how to run tests include:
    - `Cargo.toml` (workspace root)
    - `Makefile` and `Makefile.core.mk` (common build and test orchestration)
    - `build.rs` (build script)
    - `.cargo/config.toml` (Cargo configuration)

## Implementation Plan
1.  **Create a new module `src/proxy/connection_manager.rs`**:
        - Define a `ConnectionManager` struct that owns a shared `Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Connection, ConnectionDrain>>>`.
        - Define a private `ConnectionDrain` struct containing:
          - `tx: drain::Signal` and `rx: drain::Watch` for signaling close to subscribed tasks.
          - `count: usize` to track the number of active connection tasks.
        - Implement methods on `ConnectionManager`:
          - `new()`: Initializes an empty map.
          - `register(&self, c: &Connection)`: Inserts a new `ConnectionDrain` for the connection if not present.
          - `track(&self, c: &Connection) -> Option<drain::Watch>`: Increments the count for the connection and returns a clone of its `drain::Watch`. Returns `None` if the connection was not registered.
          - `release(&self, c: &Connection)`: Decrements the count for the connection. If the count reaches zero, removes the connection from the map and initiates a drain on its signal.
          - `drain(&self, conn: &Connection)`: Initiates a drain and waits for all tasks tracking that connection to release.
          - `drain_all(&self)`: Initiates a drain for all tracked connections.
          - `clear(&self)`: Removes all tracked connections without draining.
        - Add a public `pub(crate) async fn policy_watcher(state: DemandProxyState, mut updates: watch::Receiver<()>, cm: ConnectionManager, scope: &str)` function. This task:
          - Subscribes to the policy update channel.
          - When a notification is received, iterates over all currently tracked connections.
          - For each connection, calls `state.assert_rbac(&conn).await`.
          - If a connection is now denied, calls `cm.drain(conn).await` to close it.
  `    2.  **Define ordering for `Connection` in `src/rbac.rs`**:
        - Derive `Eq`, `Hash`, `Ord`, `PartialEq`, `PartialOrd` for the `Connection` struct. This is needed for sorting or using connections as keys in ordered/map structures.
    3.  **Define ordering for `Identity` in `src/identity/manager.rs`**:
        - Derive `PartialOrd` and `Ord` for the `Identity` enum to satisfy the `Ord` bound required by `Connection`.

Ensure this is called even if some configurations in a batch were rejected, as long as at least one update was accepted.

        - Add a `connection_manager: ConnectionManager` field to the `Inbound` struct and initialize it in `new()`.
        - In the `run()` method, spawn a `policy_watcher` task before the main accept loop.

192:                                         }
193:                                     }
194:                                     Err(e) => {
195:                                         error!(dur=?start.elapsed(), "internal server copy: {}", e)
196:                                     }
197:                                 }
198:                             }
199:                             Hbone(req) => match hyper::upgrade::on(req).await {
200:                                 Ok(mut upgraded) => {
201:                                     if let Err(e) = super::copy_hbone(
202:                                         &mut upgraded,
203:                                         &mut stream,
204:                                         &metrics,
205:                                         transferred_bytes,
206:                                     )
207:                                     .instrument(trace_span!("hbone server"))
208:                                     .await
209:                                     {
210:                                         error!(dur=?start.elapsed(), "hbone server copy: {}", e);
211:                                     }
212:                                 }
213:                                 Err(e) => {
214:                                     // Not sure if this can even happen
215:                                     error!(dur=?start.elapsed(), "No upgrade {e}");
216:                                 }
217:                             },
218:                         }
219:                     })
220:                     .in_current_span(),
221:                 );
222:                 // Send back our 200. We do this regardless of if our spawned task copies the data;
223:                 // we need to respond with headers immediately once connection is established for the
224:                 // stream of bytes to begin.
225:                 Ok(())
226:             }
227:         }
228:     }

232:             .get(TRACEPARENT_HEADER)

234:             .and_then(|b| TraceParent::try_from(b).ok())

243:     async fn serve_connect(
244:         state: DemandProxyState,
245:         conn: Connection,
246:         enable_original_source: bool,
247:         req: Request<Incoming>,
248:         metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
249:     ) -> Result<Response<Empty<Bytes>>, hyper::Error> {
250:         match req.method() {
251:             &Method::CONNECT => {
252:                 let uri = req.uri();
253:                 info!("got {} request to {}", req.method(), uri);
254:                 let addr: Result<SocketAddr, _> = uri.to_string().as_str().parse();
255:                 if addr.is_err() {
256:                     info!("Sending 400, {:?}", addr.err());
257:                     return Ok(Response::builder()
258:                         .status(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)
259:                         .body(Empty::new())
260:                         .unwrap());
261:                 }
262: 
263:                 let addr: SocketAddr = addr.unwrap();
264:                 if addr.ip() != conn.dst.ip() {
265:                     info!("Sending 400, ip mismatch {addr} != {}", conn.dst);
266:                     return Ok(Response::builder()
267:                         .status(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)
268:                         .body(Empty::new())
269:                         .unwrap());
270:                 }
271:                 // Orig has 15008, swap with the real port
272:                 let conn = Connection { dst: addr, ..conn };
273:                 let dst_network_addr = NetworkAddress {
274:                     network: conn.dst_network.to_string(), // dst must be on our network
275:                     address: addr.ip(),
276:                 };
277:                 let Some((upstream, upstream_service)) =
278:                     state.fetch_workload_services(&dst_network_addr).await
279:                 else {
280:                     info!(%conn, "unknown destination");
281:                     return Ok(Response::builder()
282:                         .status(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND)
283:                         .body(Empty::new())
284:                         .unwrap());
285:                 };
286:                 let has_waypoint = upstream.waypoint.is_some();
287:                 let from_waypoint = Self::check_waypoint(state.clone(), &upstream, &conn).await;
288:                 let from_gateway = Self::check_gateway(state.clone(), &upstream, &conn).await;
289: 
290:                 if from_gateway {
291:                     debug!("request from gateway");
292:                 }
293:                 if from_waypoint {
294:                     debug!("request from waypoint, skipping policy");
295:                 } else if !state.assert_rbac(&conn).await {
296:                     info!(%conn, "RBAC rejected");
297:                     return Ok(Response::builder()
298:                         .status(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
299:                         .body(Empty::new())
300:                         .unwrap());
301:                 }
302:                 if has_waypoint && !from_waypoint {
303:                     info!(%conn, "bypassed waypoint");
304:                     return Ok(Response::builder()
305:                         .status(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
306:                         .body(Empty::new())
307:                         .unwrap());
308:                 }
309:                 let source_ip = if from_waypoint {
310:                     // If the request is from our waypoint, trust the Forwarded header.
311:                     // For other request types, we can only trust the source from the connection.
312:                     // Since our own waypoint is in the same trust domain though, we can use Forwarded,
313:                     // which drops the requirement of spoofing IPs from waypoints
314:                     super::get_original_src_from_fwded(&req).unwrap_or(conn.src_ip)
315:                 } else {
316:                     conn.src_ip
317:                 };
318: 
319:                 let baggage =
320:                     parse_baggage_header(req.headers().get_all(BAGGAGE_HEADER)).unwrap_or_default();
321: 
322:                 let source = match from_gateway {
323:                     true => None, // we cannot lookup source workload since we don't know the network, see https://github.com/istio/ztunnel/issues/515
324:                     false => {
325:                         let src_network_addr = NetworkAddress {
326:                             // we can assume source network is our network because we did not traverse a gateway
327:                             network: conn.dst_network.to_string(),
328:                             address: source_ip,
329:                         };
330:                         // Find source info. We can lookup by XDS or from connection attributes
331:                         state.fetch_workload(&src_network_addr).await
332:                     }
333:                 };
334: 
335:                 let derived_source = metrics::DerivedWorkload {
336:                     identity: conn.src_identity.clone(),
337:                     cluster_id: baggage.cluster_id,
338:                     namespace: baggage.namespace,
339:                     workload_name: baggage.workload_name,
340:                     revision: baggage.revision,
341:                     ..Default::default()
342:                 };
343:                 let ds = proxy::guess_inbound_service(&conn, upstream_service, &upstream);
344:                 let connection_metrics = ConnectionOpen {
345:                     reporter: Reporter::destination,
346:                     source,
347:                     derived_source: Some(derived_source),
348:                     destination: Some(upstream),
349:                     connection_security_policy: metrics::SecurityPolicy::mutual_tls,
350:                     destination_service: ds,
351:                 };
352:                 let status_code = match Self::handle_inbound(
353:                     Hbone(req),
354:                     enable_original_source.then_some(source_ip),
355:                     addr,
356:                     metrics,
357:                     connection_metrics,
358:                     None,
359:                 )
360:                 .in_current_span()
361:                 .await
362:                 {
363:                     Ok(_) => StatusCode::OK,
364:                     Err(_) => StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
365:                 };
366: 
367:                 Ok(Response::builder()
368:                     .status(status_code)
369:                     .body(Empty::new())
370:                     .unwrap())
371:             }
372:             // Return the 404 Not Found for other routes.
373:             method => {
374:                 info!("Sending 404, got {method}");
375:                 Ok(Response::builder()
376:                     .status(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND)
377:                     .body(Empty::new())
378:                     .unwrap())
379:             }
380:         }
381:     }

383:     async fn check_waypoint(
384:         state: DemandProxyState,
385:         upstream: &Workload,
386:         conn: &Connection,
387:     ) -> bool {
388:         Self::check_gateway_address(state, conn, upstream.waypoint.as_ref()).await
389:     }
390: 
391:     async fn check_gateway(
392:         state: DemandProxyState,
393:         upstream: &Workload,
394:         conn: &Connection,
395:     ) -> bool {
396:         Self::check_gateway_address(state, conn, upstream.network_gateway.as_ref()).await
397:     }

399:     async fn check_gateway_address(
400:         state: DemandProxyState,
401:         conn: &Connection,
402:         gateway_address: Option<&GatewayAddress>,
403:     ) -> bool {
404:         if let Some(gateway_address) = gateway_address {
405:             let from_gateway = match state.fetch_destination(&gateway_address.destination).await {
406:                 Some(address::Address::Workload(wl)) => Some(wl.identity()) == conn.src_identity,
407:                 Some(address::Address::Service(svc)) => {
408:                     for (_ep_uid, ep) in svc.endpoints.iter() {
409:                         // fetch workloads by workload UID since we may not have an IP for an endpoint (e.g., endpoint is just a hostname)
410:                         if state
411:                             .fetch_workload_by_uid(&ep.workload_uid)
412:                             .await
413:                             .map(|w| w.identity())
414:                             == conn.src_identity
415:                         {
416:                             return true;
417:                         }
418:                     }
419:                     false
420:                 }
421:                 None => false,
422:             };
423:             return from_gateway;
424:         }
425:         false // this occurs if gateway_address was None
426:     }
427: }

469:                 .identity()

472:             destination=?orig_dst_addr,

476:         let cert = self.cert_manager.fetch_certificate(&identity).await?;
477:         let acc = cert.mtls_acceptor(Some(&identity))?;
478:         Ok(acc)

29: pub(super) struct InboundPassthrough {
30:     listener: TcpListener,
31:     pi: ProxyInputs,
32: }
33: 
34: impl InboundPassthrough {
35:     pub(super) async fn new(mut pi: ProxyInputs) -> Result<InboundPassthrough, Error> {
36:         let listener: TcpListener = TcpListener::bind(pi.cfg.inbound_plaintext_addr)
37:             .await
38:             .map_err(|e| Error::Bind(pi.cfg.inbound_plaintext_addr, e))?;
39:         let transparent = super::maybe_set_transparent(&pi, &listener)?;
40:         // Override with our explicitly configured setting
41:         pi.cfg.enable_original_source = Some(transparent);
42: 
43:         info!(
44:             address=%listener.local_addr().unwrap(),
45:             component="inbound plaintext",
46:             transparent,
47:             "listener established",
48:         );
49:         Ok(InboundPassthrough { listener, pi })
50:     }
51: 
52:     pub(super) async fn run(self) {
53:         loop {
54:             // Asynchronously wait for an inbound socket.
55:             let socket = self.listener.accept().await;
56:             let pi = self.pi.clone();
57:             match socket {
58:                 Ok((stream, remote)) => {
59:                     tokio::spawn(async move {
60:                         if let Err(e) = Self::proxy_inbound_plaintext(
61:                             pi, // pi cloned above; OK to move
62:                             socket::to_canonical(remote),
63:                             stream,
64:                         )
65:                         .await
66:                         {
67:                             warn!(source=%socket::to_canonical(remote), component="inbound plaintext", "proxying failed: {}", e)
68:                         }
69:                     }.in_current_span());
70:                 }
71:                 Err(e) => {
72:                     if util::is_runtime_shutdown(&e) {
73:                         return;
74:                     }
75:                     error!("Failed TCP handshake {}", e);
76:                 }
77:             }
78:         }
79:     }
80: 
81:     async fn proxy_inbound_plaintext(
82:         pi: ProxyInputs,
83:         source: SocketAddr,
84:         mut inbound: TcpStream,
85:     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
86:         let orig = socket::orig_dst_addr_or_default(&inbound);
87:         // Check if it is a recursive call when proxy mode is Node.
88:         if pi.cfg.proxy_mode == ProxyMode::Shared && Some(orig.ip()) == pi.cfg.local_ip {
89:             return Err(Error::SelfCall);
90:         }
91:         info!(%source, destination=%orig, component="inbound plaintext", "accepted connection");
92:         let network_addr = NetworkAddress {
93:             network: pi.cfg.network.clone(), // inbound request must be on our network
94:             address: orig.ip(),
95:         };
96:         let Some((upstream, upstream_service)) =
97:             pi.state.fetch_workload_services(&network_addr).await
98:         else {
99:             return Err(Error::UnknownDestination(orig.ip()));
100:         };
101:         if upstream.waypoint.is_some() {
102:             // This is an inbound request not over HBONE, but we have a waypoint.
103:             // The request needs to go through the waypoint for policy enforcement.
104:             // This can happen from clients that are not part of the mesh; they won't know to send
105:             // to the waypoint.
106:             // To handle this, we forward it to the waypoint ourselves, which will hairpin back to us.
107:             let mut oc = OutboundConnection {
108:                 pi: pi.clone(),
109:                 id: TraceParent::new(),
110:             };
111:             // Spoofing the source IP only works when the destination or the source are on our node.
112:             // In this case, the source and the destination might both be remote, so we need to disable it.
113:             oc.pi.cfg.enable_original_source = Some(false);
114:             return oc.proxy_to(inbound, source.ip(), orig, false).await;
115:         }
116: 
117:         // We enforce RBAC only for non-hairpin cases. This is because we may not be able to properly
118:         // enforce the policy (for example, if it has L7 attributes), while waypoint will.
119:         // Instead, we skip enforcement and forward to the waypoint to enforce.
120:         // On the inbound HBONE side, we will validate it came from the waypoint (and therefor had enforcemen).
121:         let conn = rbac::Connection {
122:             src_identity: None,
123:             src_ip: source.ip(),
124:             // inbound request must be on our network since this is passthrough
125:             // rather than HBONE, which can be tunneled across networks through gateways.
126:             // by definition, without the gateway our source must be on our network.
127:             dst_network: pi.cfg.network.clone(),
128:             dst: orig,
129:         };

47: impl Outbound {
48:     pub(super) async fn new(mut pi: ProxyInputs, drain: Watch) -> Result<Outbound, Error> {
49:         let listener: TcpListener = TcpListener::bind(pi.cfg.outbound_addr)
50:             .await
51:             .map_err(|e| Error::Bind(pi.cfg.outbound_addr, e))?;
52:         let transparent = super::maybe_set_transparent(&pi, &listener)?;
53:         // Override with our explicitly configured setting
54:         pi.cfg.enable_original_source = Some(transparent);
55: 
56:         info!(
57:             address=%listener.local_addr().unwrap(),
58:             component="outbound",
59:             transparent,
60:             "listener established",
61:         );
62:         Ok(Outbound {
63:             pi,
64:             listener,
65:             drain,
66:         })
67:     }

69:     pub(super) fn address(&self) -> SocketAddr {
70:         self.listener.local_addr().unwrap()
71:     }
72: 
73:     pub(super) async fn run(self) {
74:         let accept = async move {
75:             loop {
76:                 // Asynchronously wait for an inbound socket.
77:                 let socket = self.listener.accept().await;
78:                 let start_outbound_instant = Instant::now();
79:                 match socket {
80:                     Ok((stream, _remote)) => {
81:                         let mut oc = OutboundConnection {
82:                             pi: self.pi.clone(),
83:                             id: TraceParent::new(),
84:                         };
85:                         let span = info_span!("outbound", id=%oc.id);
86:                         tokio::spawn(
87:                             (async move {
88:                                 let res = oc.proxy(stream).await;
89:                                 match res {
90:                                     Ok(_) => info!(dur=?start_outbound_instant.elapsed(), "complete"),
91:                                     Err(e) => warn!(dur=?start_outbound_instant.elapsed(), err=%e, "failed")
92:                                 };
93:                             })
94:                             .instrument(span),
95:                         );
96:                     }
97:                     Err(e) => {
98:                         if util::is_runtime_shutdown(&e) {
99:                             return;
100:                         }
101:                         error!("Failed TCP handshake {}", e);
102:                     }
103:                 }
104:             }
105:         }.in_current_span();
106: 
107:         // Stop accepting once we drain.
108:         // Note: we are *not* waiting for all connections to be closed. In the future, we may consider
109:         // this, but will need some timeout period, as we have no back-pressure mechanism on connections.
110:         tokio::select! {
111:             res = accept => { res }
112:             _ = self.drain.signaled() => {
113:                 info!("outbound drained");
114:             }
115:         }
116:     }
117: }

131:     pub async fn proxy_to(
132:         &mut self,
133:         mut stream: TcpStream,

135:         orig_dst_addr: SocketAddr,

137:     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
138:         if self.pi.cfg.proxy_mode == ProxyMode::Shared
139:             && Some(orig_dst_addr.ip()) == self.pi.cfg.local_ip
140:         {
141:             return Err(Error::SelfCall);
142:         }
143:         let req = self.build_request(remote_addr, orig_dst_addr).await?;
144:         debug!(
145:             "request from {} to {} via {} type {:#?} dir {:#?}",
146:             req.source.name, orig_dst_addr, req.gateway, req.request_type, req.direction
147:         );
148:         if block_passthrough && req.destination_workload.is_none() {
149:             // This is mostly used by socks5. For typical outbound calls, we need to allow calls to arbitrary
150:             // domains. But for socks5
151:             return Err(Error::UnknownDestination(req.destination.ip()));

153:         let can_fastpath = self.pi.cfg.proxy_mode == ProxyMode::Shared
154:             && req.protocol == Protocol::HBONE
155:             && !req
156:                 .destination_workload
157:                 .as_ref()
158:                 .map(|w| w.native_tunnel)
159:                 .unwrap_or(false);
160:         let connection_metrics = metrics::ConnectionOpen {
161:             reporter: Reporter::source,
162:             derived_source: None,
163:             source: Some(req.source.clone()),
164:             destination: req.destination_workload.clone(),
165:             connection_security_policy: if req.protocol == Protocol::HBONE {
166:                 metrics::SecurityPolicy::mutual_tls
167:             } else {
168:                 metrics::SecurityPolicy::unknown
169:             },
170:             destination_service: req.destination_service.clone(),
171:         };

173:         if req.request_type == RequestType::DirectLocal && can_fastpath {
174:             // For same node, we just access it directly rather than making a full network connection.
175:             // Pass our `stream` over to the inbound handler, which will process as usual
176:             // We *could* apply this to all traffic, rather than just for destinations that are "captured"
177:             // However, we would then get inconsistent behavior where only node-local pods have RBAC enforced.
178:             info!("proxying to {} using node local fast path", req.destination);
179:             let origin_src = if self.pi.cfg.enable_original_source.unwrap_or_default() {
180:                 super::get_original_src_from_stream(&stream)
181:             } else {
182:                 None
183:             };
184:             let conn = rbac::Connection {
185:                 src_identity: Some(req.source.identity()),
186:                 src_ip: remote_addr,
187:                 dst_network: req.source.network.clone(), // since this is node local, it's the same network
188:                 dst: req.destination,
189:             };
190:             if !self.pi.state.assert_rbac(&conn).await {
191:                 info!(%conn, "RBAC rejected");
192:                 return Err(Error::HttpStatus(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED));
193:             }
194:             // same as above but inverted, this is the "inbound" metric
195:             let inbound_connection_metrics = metrics::ConnectionOpen {
196:                 reporter: Reporter::destination,
197:                 derived_source: None,
198:                 source: Some(req.source.clone()),
199:                 destination: req.destination_workload.clone(),
200:                 connection_security_policy: if req.protocol == Protocol::HBONE {
201:                     metrics::SecurityPolicy::mutual_tls
202:                 } else {
203:                     metrics::SecurityPolicy::unknown
204:                 },
205:                 destination_service: req.destination_service,
206:             };
207:             return Inbound::handle_inbound(
208:                 InboundConnect::DirectPath(stream),
209:                 origin_src,
210:                 req.destination,
211:                 self.pi.metrics.to_owned(), // self is a borrow so this clone is to return an owned
212:                 connection_metrics,
213:                 Some(inbound_connection_metrics),
214:             )
215:             .await
216:             .map_err(Error::Io);
217:         }
218: 
219:         let transferred_bytes = metrics::BytesTransferred::from(&connection_metrics);
220: 
221:         // _connection_close will record once dropped
222:         let _connection_close = self
223:             .pi
224:             .metrics
225:             .increment_defer::<_, metrics::ConnectionClose>(&connection_metrics);
226:         match req.protocol {
227:             Protocol::HBONE => {
228:                 info!(
229:                     "proxy to {} using HBONE via {} type {:#?}",
230:                     req.destination, req.gateway, req.request_type
231:                 );
232: 
233:                 let mut allowed_sans: Vec<Identity> = Vec::new();
234:                 for san in req.upstream_sans.iter() {
235:                     match Identity::from_str(san) {
236:                         Ok(ident) => allowed_sans.push(ident.clone()),

244:                 let dst_identity = allowed_sans;

246:                 let pool_key = pool::Key {

252:                 // Setup our connection future. This won't always run if we have an existing connection

255:                     let mut builder =
256:                         hyper::client::conn::http2::Builder::new(hyper_util::TokioExecutor);
257:                     let builder = builder
258:                         .initial_stream_window_size(self.pi.cfg.window_size)

263:                         .pi

291:                 let mut f = http_types::proxies::Forwarded::new();
292:                 f.add_for(remote_addr.to_string());
293: 
294:                 let request = hyper::Request::builder()
295:                     .uri(&req.destination.to_string())
296:                     .method(hyper::Method::CONNECT)
297:                     .version(hyper::Version::HTTP_2)

299:                         BAGGAGE_HEADER,
300:                         baggage(&req, self.pi.cfg.cluster_id.clone()),
301:                     )

307:                 let response = connection.send_request(request).await?;

309:                 let code = response.status();
310:                 if code != 200 {
311:                     return Err(Error::HttpStatus(code));
312:                 }
313:                 let mut upgraded = hyper::upgrade::on(response).await?;
314: 
315:                 super::copy_hbone(
316:                     &mut upgraded,
317:                     &mut stream,
318:                     &self.pi.metrics,
319:                     transferred_bytes,
320:                 )
321:                 .instrument(trace_span!("hbone client"))

323:             }

325:                 info!(
326:                     "Proxying to {} using TCP via {} type {:?}",
327:                     req.destination, req.gateway, req.request_type
328:                 );
329:                 // Create a TCP connection to upstream
330:                 let local = if self.pi.cfg.enable_original_source.unwrap_or_default() {
331:                     super::get_original_src_from_stream(&stream)

333:                     None
334:                 };
335:                 let mut outbound = super::freebind_connect(local, req.gateway).await?;

338:                     &mut stream,

349:     async fn build_request(
350:         &self,
351:         downstream: IpAddr,
352:         target: SocketAddr,
353:     ) -> Result<Request, Error> {
354:         let downstream_network_addr = NetworkAddress {
355:             network: self.pi.cfg.network.clone(),
356:             address: downstream,
357:         };
358:         let source_workload = match self.pi.state.fetch_workload(&downstream_network_addr).await {
359:             Some(wl) => wl,
360:             None => return Err(Error::UnknownSource(downstream)),
361:         };
362: 
363:         // TODO: we want a single lock for source and upstream probably...?
364:         let us = self
365:             .pi
366:             .state
367:             .fetch_upstream(&source_workload.network, target)
368:             .await;
369:         if us.is_none() {
370:             // For case no upstream found, passthrough it
371:             return Ok(Request {
372:                 protocol: Protocol::TCP,
373:                 source: source_workload,
374:                 destination: target,
375:                 destination_workload: None,
376:                 destination_service: None,
377:                 expected_identity: None,
378:                 gateway: target,
379:                 direction: Direction::Outbound,
380:                 request_type: RequestType::Passthrough,
381:                 upstream_sans: vec![],
382:             });
383:         }
384: 
385:         let mut mutable_us = us.unwrap();
386:         let workload_ip = self
387:             .pi
388:             .state
389:             .load_balance(
390:                 &mutable_us.workload,
391:                 &source_workload,
392:                 self.pi.metrics.clone(),
393:             )
394:             .await?;
395: 
396:         // For case upstream server has enabled waypoint
397:         match self
398:             .pi
399:             .state
400:             .fetch_waypoint(&mutable_us.workload, workload_ip)
401:             .await
402:         {
403:             Ok(None) => {} // workload doesn't have a waypoint; this is fine
404:             Ok(Some(waypoint_us)) => {
405:                 let waypoint_workload = waypoint_us.workload;
406:                 let waypoint_ip = self
407:                     .pi
408:                     .state
409:                     .load_balance(
410:                         &waypoint_workload,
411:                         &source_workload,
412:                         self.pi.metrics.clone(),
413:                     )
414:                     .await?;
415:                 let wp_socket_addr = SocketAddr::new(waypoint_ip, waypoint_us.port);
416:                 return Ok(Request {
417:                     // Always use HBONE here
418:                     protocol: Protocol::HBONE,
419:                     source: source_workload,
420:                     // Use the original VIP, not translated
421:                     destination: target,
422:                     destination_workload: Some(mutable_us.workload),
423:                     destination_service: mutable_us.destination_service.clone(),
424:                     expected_identity: Some(waypoint_workload.identity()),
425:                     gateway: wp_socket_addr,
426:                     // Let the client remote know we are on the inbound path.
427:                     direction: Direction::Inbound,
428:                     request_type: RequestType::ToServerWaypoint,
429:                     upstream_sans: mutable_us.sans,
430:                 });
431:             }
432:             // we expected the workload to have a waypoint, but could not find one
433:             Err(e) => return Err(Error::UnknownWaypoint(e.to_string())),
434:         }
435: 
436:         let us = match set_gateway_address(&mut mutable_us, workload_ip, self.pi.hbone_port) {
437:             Ok(_) => mutable_us,
438:             Err(e) => {
439:                 debug!(%mutable_us.workload.workload_name, "failed to set gateway address for upstream: {}", e);
440:                 return Err(Error::UnknownWaypoint(mutable_us.workload.workload_name));
441:             }
442:         };
443: 
444:         if us.workload.gateway_address.is_none() {
445:             return Err(Error::NoGatewayAddress(Box::new(us.workload)));
446:         }
447: 
448:         // For case source client and upstream server are on the same node
449:         if !us.workload.node.is_empty()
450:             && self.pi.cfg.local_node.as_ref() == Some(&us.workload.node) // looks weird but in Rust borrows can be compared and will behave the same as owned (https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.reference.html)
451:             && us.workload.protocol == Protocol::HBONE
452:         {
453:             trace!(
454:                 workload_node = us.workload.node,
455:                 local_node = self.pi.cfg.local_node,
456:                 "select {:?}",
457:                 RequestType::DirectLocal
458:             );
459:             return Ok(Request {
460:                 protocol: Protocol::HBONE,
461:                 source: source_workload,
462:                 destination: SocketAddr::from((workload_ip, us.port)),
463:                 destination_workload: Some(us.workload.clone()),
464:                 destination_service: us.destination_service.clone(),
465:                 expected_identity: Some(us.workload.identity()),
466:                 gateway: SocketAddr::from((
467:                     us.workload
468:                         .gateway_address
469:                         .expect("gateway address confirmed")
470:                         .ip(),
471:                     self.pi.hbone_port,
472:                 )),
473:                 direction: Direction::Outbound,
474:                 // Sending to a node on the same node (ourselves).
475:                 // In the future this could be optimized to avoid a full network traversal.
476:                 request_type: RequestType::DirectLocal,
477:                 upstream_sans: us.sans,
478:             });
479:         }
480:         // For case no waypoint for both side and direct to remote node proxy
481:         Ok(Request {
482:             protocol: us.workload.protocol,
483:             source: source_workload,
484:             destination: SocketAddr::from((workload_ip, us.port)),
485:             destination_workload: Some(us.workload.clone()),
486:             destination_service: us.destination_service.clone(),
487:             expected_identity: Some(us.workload.identity()),
488:             gateway: us
489:                 .workload
490:                 .gateway_address
491:                 .expect("gateway address confirmed"),
492:             direction: Direction::Outbound,
493:             request_type: RequestType::Direct,
494:             upstream_sans: us.sans,
495:         })
496:     }
497: }

501:             namespace = r.source.namespace,
502:             workload_type = r.source.workload_type,
503:             workload_name = r.source.workload_name,
504:             name = r.source.canonical_name,

35: impl Socks5 {
36:     pub(super) async fn new(pi: ProxyInputs, drain: Watch) -> Result<Socks5, Error> {
37:         let listener: TcpListener = TcpListener::bind(pi.cfg.socks5_addr)
38:             .await
39:             .map_err(|e| Error::Bind(pi.cfg.socks5_addr, e))?;

41:         info!(
42:             address=%listener.local_addr().unwrap(),
43:             component="socks5",

49:             listener,

55:         self.listener.local_addr().unwrap()
56:     }
57: 
58:     pub async fn run(self) {
59:         let accept = async move {
60:             loop {
61:                 // Asynchronously wait for an inbound socket.
62:                 let socket = self.listener.accept().await;
63:                 match socket {
64:                     Ok((stream, remote)) => {
65:                         info!("accepted outbound connection from {}", remote);
66:                         let oc = OutboundConnection {
67:                             pi: self.pi.clone(),
68:                             id: TraceParent::new(),
69:                         };
70:                         tokio::spawn(async move {
71:                             if let Err(err) = handle(oc, stream).await {
72:                                 log::error!("handshake error: {}", err);
73:                             }
74:                         });
75:                     }
76:                     Err(e) => {
77:                         if util::is_runtime_shutdown(&e) {
78:                             return;
79:                         }
80:                         error!("Failed TCP handshake {}", e);
81:                     }
82:                 }
83:             }
84:         };
85: 
86:         tokio::select! {
87:             res = accept => { res }
88:             _ = self.drain.signaled() => {
89:                 info!("socks5 drained");
90:             }
91:         }
92:     }
93: }

95: // handle will process a SOCKS5 connection. This supports a minimal subset of the protocol,
96: // sufficient to integrate with common clients:
97: // - only unauthenticated requests
98: // - only CONNECT, with IPv4 or IPv6
99: async fn handle(mut oc: OutboundConnection, mut stream: TcpStream) -> Result<(), anyhow::Error> {
100:     // Version(5), Number of auth methods
101:     let mut version = [0u8; 2];
102:     stream.read_exact(&mut version).await?;
103: 
104:     if version[0] != 0x05 {
105:         return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Invalid version"));
106:     }
107: 
108:     let nmethods = version[1];
109: 
110:     if nmethods == 0 {
111:         return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Invalid auth methods"));
112:     }
113: 
114:     // List of supported auth methods
115:     let mut methods = vec![0u8; nmethods as usize];
116:     stream.read_exact(&mut methods).await?;
117: 
118:     // Client must include 'unauthenticated' (0).
119:     if !methods.into_iter().any(|x| x == 0) {
120:         return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unsupported auth method"));
121:     }
122: 
123:     // Select 'unauthenticated' (0).
124:     stream.write_all(&[0x05, 0x00]).await?;
125: 
126:     // Version(5), Command - only support CONNECT (1)
127:     let mut version_command = [0u8; 2];
128:     stream.read_exact(&mut version_command).await?;
129:     let version = version_command[0];
130: 
131:     if version != 0x05 {
132:         return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unsupported version"));
133:     }
134: 
135:     if version_command[1] != 1 {
136:         return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unsupported command"));
137:     }
138: 
139:     // Skip RSV
140:     stream.read_exact(&mut [0]).await?;
141: 
142:     // Address type
143:     let mut atyp = [0u8];
144:     stream.read_exact(&mut atyp).await?;
145: 
146:     let ip;
147: 
148:     match atyp[0] {
149:         0x01 => {
150:             let mut hostb = [0u8; 4];
151:             stream.read_exact(&mut hostb).await?;
152:             ip = IpAddr::V4(hostb.into());
153:         }
154:         0x04 => {
155:             let mut hostb = [0u8; 16];
156:             stream.read_exact(&mut hostb).await?;
157:             ip = IpAddr::V6(hostb.into());
158:         }
159:         0x03 => {
160:             let mut domain_length = [0u8];
161:             stream.read_exact(&mut domain_length).await?;
162:             let mut domain = vec![0u8; domain_length[0] as usize];
163:             stream.read_exact(&mut domain).await?;
164:             // TODO: DNS lookup, if we want to integrate with HTTP-based apps without
165:             // a DNS server.
166:             return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unsupported host"));
167:         }
168:         _ => {
169:             return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unsupported host"));
170:         }
171:     };
172: 
173:     let mut port = [0u8; 2];
174:     stream.read_exact(&mut port).await?;
175:     let port = BigEndian::read_u16(&port);
176: 
177:     let host = SocketAddr::new(ip, port);
178: 
179:     let remote_addr = socket::to_canonical(stream.peer_addr().expect("must receive peer addr"));
180: 
181:     // Send dummy values - the client generally ignores it.
182:     let buf = [
183:         0x05u8, // versuib
184:         0x00, 0x00, // success, rsv
185:         0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // IPv4
186:         0x00, 0x00, // port
187:     ];
188:     stream.write_all(&buf).await?;
189: 
190:     info!("accepted connection from {remote_addr} to {host}");
191:     tokio::spawn(async move {
192:         let res = oc.proxy_to(stream, remote_addr.ip(), host, true).await;
193:         match res {
194:             Ok(_) => {}
195:             Err(ref e) => warn!("outbound proxy failed: {}", e),
196:         };
197:     });
198:     Ok(())
199: }

244: impl StringMatch {
245:     pub fn matches_principal(&self, check: &str) -> bool {
246:         // Istio matches all assumes spiffe:// prefix. This includes prefix matches.
247:         // A prefix match for "*foo" means "spiffe://*foo".
248:         // So we strip it, and fail if it isn't present.
249:         let Some(check) = check.strip_prefix("spiffe://") else {
250:             return false;
251:         };
252:         self.matches(check)
253:     }

255:     pub fn matches(&self, check: &str) -> bool {
256:         match self {
257:             StringMatch::Prefix(pre) => check.starts_with(pre),
258:             StringMatch::Suffix(suf) => check.ends_with(suf),
259:             StringMatch::Exact(exact) => exact == check,
260:             StringMatch::Presence() => !check.is_empty(),
261:         }
262:     }
263: }

18: /// A PolicyStore encapsulates all policy information about workloads in the mesh
19: #[derive(serde::Serialize, Default, Debug)]
20: pub struct PolicyStore {
21:     /// policies maintains a mapping of ns/name to policy.
22:     by_key: HashMap<String, Authorization>,
23: 
24:     /// policies_by_namespace maintains a mapping of namespace (or "" for global) to policy names
25:     by_namespace: HashMap<String, HashSet<String>>,
26: }
27: 
28: impl PolicyStore {
29:     pub fn get<T: AsRef<str>>(&self, key: T) -> Option<&Authorization> {
30:         self.by_key.get(key.as_ref())
31:     }
32: 
33:     pub fn get_by_namespace<T: AsRef<str>>(&self, namespace: T) -> Vec<String> {
34:         self.by_namespace
35:             .get(namespace.as_ref())
36:             .into_iter()
37:             .flatten()
38:             .cloned()
39:             .collect()
40:     }
41: 
42:     pub fn insert(&mut self, rbac: Authorization) {
43:         let key = rbac.to_key();
44:         match rbac.scope {
45:             RbacScope::Global => {
46:                 self.by_namespace
47:                     .entry("".to_string())
48:                     .or_default()
49:                     .insert(key.clone());
50:             }
51:             RbacScope::Namespace => {
52:                 self.by_namespace
53:                     .entry(rbac.namespace.clone())
54:                     .or_default()
55:                     .insert(key.clone());
56:             }
57:             RbacScope::WorkloadSelector => {}
58:         }
59:         self.by_key.insert(key, rbac);
60:     }
61: 
62:     pub fn remove(&mut self, name: String) {
63:         let Some(rbac) = self.by_key.remove(&name) else {
64:             return;
65:         };
66:         if let Some(key) = match rbac.scope {

183:         client: Box<dyn CaClientTrait>,

185:         cfg: SecretManagerConfig,

187:         if cfg.concurrency == 0 {
188:             panic!("concurrency cannot be 0, operations would block forever");

190:         let worker = Arc::new(Self {

192:             time_conv: cfg.time_conv,

197:         // Process requests in the background. The task will terminate on its own when the
198:         // identities channel is dropped.

203:     async fn has_id(&self, id: &Identity) -> bool {

209:     async fn run(&self, mut requests: mpsc::Receiver<Request>) {
210:         use futures::stream::FuturesUnordered;
211:         use futures::StreamExt;
212:         use priority_queue::PriorityQueue;
213: 
214:         #[derive(Eq, PartialEq)]
215:         enum Fetch {
216:             Processing,
217:             Forgetting,
218:         }
219: 
220:         // A set of futures refreshing the certificates. Each future completes with the identity for
221:         // which it was invoked and a resulting certificate or error.
222:         let mut fetches = FuturesUnordered::new();
223:         // The set of identities for which there are pending fetches. Elements of `fetches` and
224:         // `processing` correspond to each other.
225:         let mut processing: HashMap<Identity, Fetch> = HashMap::new();
226:         // Identities for which we will need to refresh certificates in the future, ordered by the
227:         // priority and time at which the refresh needs to happen.
228:         //
229:         // Note that while the sorting criteria may seem too simple, it is in fact correct due to
230:         // the specifics of values inserted. Only Background priority items are ever inserted into
231:         // the future, for all other priorities Instant::now() is used as the scheduled time of the
232:         // refresh. In other words, at any point in time, there are no high-priority
233:         // (not Background) items scheduled to run in the future.
234:         let mut pending: PriorityQueue<Identity, PendingPriority> = PriorityQueue::new();
235: 
236:         'main: loop {
237:             let next = pending.peek().map(|(_, PendingPriority(_, ts))| *ts);
238:             tokio::select! {
239:                 // Handle requests from SecretManager. Those are generally split between the
240:                 // client-side processing (operations on the `certs` map) and the worker-side
241:                 // processing (receiving the relevant request and taking action on it). The order
242:                 // of processing of requests here may not match with the order the `certs` map was
243:                 // processed by clients: it is possible for concurrent calls fetch_certificate
244:                 // (id) and forget_certificate(id) to result in id not being present in the `certs`
245:                 // map, but the Fetch and Forget requests arriving in the reverse order in the
246:                 // worker here.
247:                 //
248:                 // For that reason, we check the `certs` map (via the has_id call) before processing
249:                 // each request to decide if it's still relevant. After the check we are free to
250:                 // not worry about ordering and proceed with handling the request - a contradicting
251:                 // call made later by the client would result in another request being delivered to
252:                 // the worker.
253:                 res = requests.recv() => match res {
254:                     Some(Request::Fetch(id, pri)) => {
255:                         if !self.has_id(&id).await {
256:                             // Nobody interested in the Identity anymore, do nothing.
257:                             continue 'main;
258:                         }
259:                         match processing.get(&id) {
260:                             None => {
261:                                 pending.push_increase(id, PendingPriority(pri, Instant::now()));
262:                             },
263:                             Some(Fetch::Forgetting) => {
264:                                 // Once the associated future completes, the result will be dropped
265:                                 // instead of communicated back to the `certs` map and queued for
266:                                 // refresh.
267:                                 processing.insert(id, Fetch::Processing);
268:                             },
269:                             Some(Fetch::Processing) => (),
270:                         }
271:                     },
272:                     Some(Request::Forget(id)) => {
273:                         if self.has_id(&id).await {
274:                             // After the forget was queued, there was another request to start
275:                             // managing the Identity. Do nothing.
276:                             continue 'main;
277:                         }
278:                         match processing.get(&id) {
279:                             None => {
280:                                 pending.remove(&id);
281:                             },
282:                             Some(Fetch::Processing) => {
283:                                 processing.insert(id, Fetch::Forgetting);
284:                             },
285:                             Some(Fetch::Forgetting) => (),
286:                         }
287:                     },
288:                     None => break 'main,
289:                 },
290:                 // Handle fetch results.
291:                 Some((id, res)) = fetches.next() => {
292:                     match processing.remove(&id) {
293:                         Some(Fetch::Processing) => (),
294:                         Some(Fetch::Forgetting) => continue 'main,
295:                         None => unreachable!("processing should represent all fetches"),
296:                     }
297:                     let (state, refresh_at) = match res {
298:                         Err(err) => {
299:                             let refresh_at = Instant::now() + CERT_REFRESH_FAILURE_RETRY_DELAY;
300:                             (CertState::Unavailable(err), refresh_at)
301:                         },
302:                         Ok(certs) => {
303:                             let certs: tls::Certs = certs; // Type annotation.
304:                             let refresh_at = self.time_conv.system_time_to_instant(certs.refresh_at());
305:                             let refresh_at = if let Some(t) = refresh_at {
306:                                 t.into()
307:                             } else {
308:                                 // Malformed certificate (not_after is way too much into the
309:                                 // past or the future). Queue another refresh soon.
310:                                 //
311:                                 // TODO: This is a bit inconsistent since we still return the
312:                                 // certificate to the caller successfully. Basically the
313:                                 // behavior is silly, but simple and avoid panics in time math.
314:                                 // We'll try to get rid of the SystemTime <-> Instant
315:                                 // conversion here, so for now leaving the code as is.
316:                                 Instant::now()
317:                             };
318:                             (CertState::Available(certs), refresh_at)
319:                         },
320:                     };
321:                     if self.update_certs(&id, state).await {
322:                         pending.push_increase(id, PendingPriority(Priority::Background, refresh_at));
323:                     }
324:                 },
325:                 // Initiate the next fetch.
326:                 true = maybe_sleep_until(next), if fetches.len() < self.concurrency as usize => {
327:                     let (id, _) = pending.pop().unwrap();
328:                     processing.insert(id.to_owned(), Fetch::Processing);
329:                     fetches.push(async move {
330:                         let res = self.client.fetch_certificate(&id).await;
331:                         (id, res)
332:                     });
333:                 },
334:             };
335:         }
336:         // SecretManager dropped, drain remaining requests and terminate background processing.
337:         while fetches.next().await.is_some() {}
338:     }

340:     // Returns whether the Identity is still managed.
341:     async fn update_certs(&self, id: &Identity, certs: CertState) -> bool {
342:         // Both errors (lack of entry in the `certs` map and a send error) are handled the same way
343:         // (by returning false): either (a) there was no entry in the `certs` map due to a
344:         // forget_certificate call some time ago or (b) a forget_certificate call was made and
345:         // finished just after the lock was released (but before certs was sent)
346:         match self.certs.lock().await.get(id) {
347:             Some(state) => {
348:                 state.tx.send(certs).expect("state.rx cannot be gone");
349:                 true
350:             }
351:             None => false,
352:         }
353:     }
354: }

379: pub struct SecretManager {

387: impl SecretManager {
388:     pub async fn new(cfg: crate::config::Config) -> Result<Self, Error> {

403:         Self::new_internal(
404:             Box::new(client),

413:     fn new_internal(
414:         client: Box<dyn CaClientTrait>,
415:         cfg: SecretManagerConfig,
416:     ) -> (Self, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>) {
417:         let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(10);

419:         (

421:                 worker,

423:             },
424:             handle,
425:         )

428:     async fn post(&self, req: Request) {
429:         if let Err(e) = self.requests.send(req).await {
430:             unreachable!("SecretManager worker died: {e}");
431:         }
432:     }
433: 
434:     async fn start_fetch(
435:         &self,
436:         id: &Identity,
437:         pri: Priority,
438:     ) -> Result<watch::Receiver<CertState>, Error> {
439:         let mut certs = self.worker.certs.lock().await;
440:         match certs.get(id) {
441:             // Identity found in cache and is already being refreshed. Bump the priority if needed.
442:             Some(st) => {
443:                 let rx = st.rx.clone();
444:                 drop(certs);
445: 
446:                 if let Some(existing_pri) = init_pri(&rx) {
447:                     if pri > existing_pri {
448:                         self.post(Request::Fetch(id.clone(), pri)).await;
449:                     }
450:                 }
451:                 Ok(rx)
452:             }
453:             // New identity, start managing it and return the newly created channel.
454:             None => {
455:                 let (tx, rx) = watch::channel(CertState::Initializing(pri));
456:                 certs.insert(id.to_owned(), CertChannel { rx: rx.clone(), tx });
457:                 drop(certs);
458:                 // Notify the background worker to start refreshing the certificate.
459:                 self.post(Request::Fetch(id.to_owned(), pri)).await;
460:                 Ok(rx)
461:             }
462:         }
463:     }
464: 
465:     async fn wait(&self, mut rx: watch::Receiver<CertState>) -> Result<tls::Certs, Error> {
466:         loop {
467:             tokio::select! {
468:                 // Wait for the initial value if not ready yet.
469:                 res = rx.changed() => match res {
470:                     Ok(()) => match *rx.borrow() {
471:                         CertState::Unavailable(ref err) => return Err(err.to_owned()),
472:                         CertState::Available(ref certs) => return Ok(certs.to_owned()),
473:                         // Another call bumped up the priority, but still fetching the first
474:                         // certificate.
475:                         CertState::Initializing(_) => (),
476:                     },
477:                     Err(_) => return Err(Error::Forgotten),
478:                 },
479:                 // Ideally we'd detect it by rx.changed() failing above, but making sure that senders
480:                 // are owned by the background worker (and so drop on panic/other error) complicates
481:                 // the code.
482:                 _ = self.requests.closed() => unreachable!("SecretManager worker died: requests channel is closed"),
483:             }
484:         }
485:     }

487:     pub async fn fetch_certificate_pri(
488:         &self,
489:         id: &Identity,
490:         pri: Priority,
491:     ) -> Result<tls::Certs, Error> {
492:         // This method is intentionally left simple, since since unit tests are based on start_fetch
493:         // and wait. Any changes should go to one of those two methods, and if that proves
494:         // impossible - unit testing strategy may need to be rethinked.
495:         self.wait(self.start_fetch(id, pri).await?).await
496:     }
497: 
498:     pub async fn fetch_certificate(&self, id: &Identity) -> Result<tls::Certs, Error> {
499:         self.fetch_certificate_pri(id, Priority::RealTime).await
500:     }
501: 
502:     pub async fn forget_certificate(&self, id: &Identity) {
503:         if self.worker.certs.lock().await.remove(id).is_some() {
504:             self.post(Request::Forget(id.clone())).await;
505:         }
506:     }

508:     // TODO(qfel): It would be much nicer to have something like map_certs returning an iterator,
509:     // but due to locking that would require a self-referential type.
510:     pub async fn collect_certs<R>(&self, f: impl Fn(&Identity, &CertState) -> R) -> Vec<R> {
511:         let mut ret = Vec::new();
512:         for (id, chan) in self.worker.certs.lock().await.iter() {
513:             ret.push(f(id, &chan.rx.borrow()));
514:         }
515:         ret
516:     }
517: }

519: // Matches CertState::Initializing(pri) from a Receiver, wrapped in a function to make borrow
520: // lifetimes more manageable.
521: fn init_pri(rx: &watch::Receiver<CertState>) -> Option<Priority> {
522:     match *rx.borrow() {
523:         CertState::Initializing(pri) => Some(pri),
524:         _ => None,

179:             // we don't have namespace/hostname xds primary key for service
180:             if expected {
181:                 warn!(
182:                     "tried to remove service keyed by {} but it did not have the expected namespace/hostname format",
183:                     xds_name
184:                 );
185:             }
186:             return;
187:         };
188: 
189:         if name.hostname.contains('/') {
190:             // avoid trying to delete obvious workload UIDs as a service,
191:             // which can result in noisy logs when new workloads are added
192:             // (we remove then add workloads on initial update)
193:             //
194:             // we can make this assumption because namespaces and hostnames cannot have `/` in them
195:             trace!(
196:                 "xds_name {} is obviously not a service, not attempting to delete as such",
197:                 xds_name
198:             );
199:             return;
200:         }
201:         if state.services.remove(&name).is_none() && expected {
202:             warn!("tried to remove service keyed by {name}, but it was not found");

288: fn service_endpoints(
289:     workload: &Workload,
290:     services: &HashMap<String, PortList>,
291: ) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<Endpoint>> {
292:     let mut out = Vec::new();
293:     for (namespaced_host, ports) in services {
294:         // Parse the namespaced hostname for the service.
295:         let namespaced_host = match namespaced_host.split_once('/') {
296:             Some((namespace, hostname)) => NamespacedHostname {
297:                 namespace: namespace.to_string(),
298:                 hostname: hostname.to_string(),
299:             },
300:             None => {
301:                 return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
302:                     "failed parsing service name: {namespaced_host}"
303:                 ));
304:             }
305:         };
306: 
307:         // Create service endpoints for all the workload IPs.
308:         for wip in &workload.workload_ips {
309:             out.push(Endpoint {
310:                 workload_uid: workload.uid.clone(),
311:                 service: namespaced_host.clone(),
312:                 address: Some(network_addr(&workload.network, *wip)),
313:                 port: ports.into(),
314:             })
315:         }
316:         if workload.workload_ips.is_empty() {
317:             out.push(Endpoint {
318:                 workload_uid: workload.uid.clone(),
319:                 service: namespaced_host.clone(),
320:                 address: None,
321:                 port: ports.into(),
322:             })
323:         }
324:     }
325:     Ok(out)

200: // TLS record size max is 16k. But we also have a H2 frame header, so leave a bit of room for that.
201: const HBONE_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 16_384 - 64;
202: 
203: pub async fn copy_hbone(
204:     upgraded: &mut hyper::upgrade::Upgraded,
205:     stream: &mut TcpStream,
206:     metrics: impl AsRef<Metrics>,
207:     transferred_bytes: BytesTransferred<'_>,
208: ) -> Result<(), Error> {
209:     use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;
210:     let (mut ri, mut wi) = tokio::io::split(hyper_util::rt::TokioIo::new(upgraded));
211:     let (mut ro, mut wo) = stream.split();
212: 
213:     let (mut sent, mut received): (u64, u64) = (0, 0);
214: 
215:     let client_to_server = async {
216:         let mut ri = tokio::io::BufReader::with_capacity(HBONE_BUFFER_SIZE, &mut ri);
217:         let res = tokio::io::copy_buf(&mut ri, &mut wo).await;
218:         trace!(?res, "hbone -> tcp");
219:         received = res?;
220:         wo.shutdown().await
221:     };
222: 
223:     let server_to_client = async {
224:         let mut ro = tokio::io::BufReader::with_capacity(HBONE_BUFFER_SIZE, &mut ro);
225:         let res = tokio::io::copy_buf(&mut ro, &mut wi).await;
226:         trace!(?res, "tcp -> hbone");
227:         sent = res?;
228:         wi.shutdown().await
229:     };
230: 
231:     tokio::try_join!(client_to_server, server_to_client)?;
232: 
233:     trace!(sent, recv = received, "copy hbone complete");
234:     metrics
235:         .as_ref()
236:         .record(&transferred_bytes, (sent, received));
237:     Ok(())
238: }

357: pub async fn freebind_connect(local: Option<IpAddr>, addr: SocketAddr) -> io::Result<TcpStream> {
358:     async fn connect(local: Option<IpAddr>, addr: SocketAddr) -> io::Result<TcpStream> {
359:         match local {
360:             None => {
361:                 trace!(dest=%addr, "no local address, connect directly");
362:                 Ok(TcpStream::connect(addr).await?)
363:             }
364:             // TODO: Need figure out how to handle case of loadbalancing to itself.
365:             //       We use ztunnel addr instead, otherwise app side will be confused.
366:             Some(src) if src == socket::to_canonical(addr).ip() => {
367:                 trace!(%src, dest=%addr, "dest and source are the same, connect directly");
368:                 Ok(TcpStream::connect(addr).await?)
369:             }
370:             Some(src) => {
371:                 let socket = if src.is_ipv4() {
372:                     TcpSocket::new_v4()?
373:                 } else {
374:                     TcpSocket::new_v6()?
375:                 };
376: 
377:                 let local_addr = SocketAddr::new(src, 0);
378:                 match socket::set_freebind_and_transparent(&socket) {
379:                     Err(err) => warn!("failed to set freebind: {:?}", err),
380:                     _ => {
381:                         if let Err(err) = socket.bind(local_addr) {
382:                             warn!("failed to bind local addr: {:?}", err)
383:                         }
384:                     }
385:                 };
386:                 trace!(%src, dest=%addr, "connect with source IP");
387:                 Ok(socket.connect(addr).await?)
388:             }
389:         }
390:     }
391:     // Wrap the entire connect function in a timeout
392:     timeout(CONNECTION_TIMEOUT, connect(local, addr))
393:         .await
394:         .map_err(|e| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::TimedOut, e))?
395: }

## New module `src/proxy/connection_manager.rs`
- `ConnectionManager` owns `Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Connection, ConnectionDrain>>>`; `ConnectionDrain` holds `tx: drain::Signal`, `rx: drain::Watch`, and `count`.
- Methods: `new/register/track/release/drain/drain_all/clear`, plus private `conns()` snapshot helper. `track` returns a `drain::Watch` clone (held for a task's lifetime); `release` removes + signals when count hits zero; `drain` removes the entry, initiates a drain, and awaits task release.

## Supporting changes
- `src/rbac.rs`: `Connection` now derives `Hash, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd` (used as map key).
- `src/identity/manager.rs`: `Identity` derives `PartialOrd, Ord`.
- `src/state/policy.rs`: `#[serde(skip)] notifier: PolicyStoreNotify` wrapping a `watch::Sender<()>`, with `Default/subscribe/send`, plus `PolicyStore::subscribe()/send()`.

145: # This function is designed for maximum compatibility with various platforms. This runs on
146: # any Mac or Linux platform with bash 4.2+. Please take care not to modify this function
147: # without testing properly.

149: # This function will properly handle any type of path including those with spaces using the

151: #
152: # testcase: "a:b c:d"
153: # testcase: "a b:c d:e f"
154: # testcase: "a b:c:d e"
155: parse_KUBECONFIG () {
156: TMPDIR=""
157: if [[ "$1" =~ ([^:]*):(.*) ]]; then
158:   while true; do
159:     rematch=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
160:     add_KUBECONFIG_if_exists "$rematch"
161:     remainder="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"

 #!/bin/bash
 # shellcheck disable=SC2034
 
 # WARNING: DO NOT EDIT, THIS FILE IS PROBABLY A COPY
 #
 # The original version of this file is located in the https://github.com/istio/common-files repo.
 # If you're looking at this file in a different repo and want to make a change, please go to the
 # common-files repo, make the change there and check it in. Then come back to this repo and run

 # Copyright Istio Authors
